item.title: He Was Going to Bleed on Me?? College student escaped knife attack and ran for help - then was shot by cops five times
item.description: A college student is suing after cops shot him five times while he tried to flee a hostage situation and knife attack in his own home. Maverick Lyon, 21, was fleeing his family's North Albany, Oregon, home after being held at knifepoint by his brother, John “Dakota” Lyon, 27, when officers opened fire on January 6. The lawsuit against the city and two cops accuses officers of mishandling the response, citing poor communication, a lack of coordination and their failure to use the father's descriptions of the brothers' clothing to distinguish the hostage from the suspected attacker. Lyon repeatedly mouthed “Help me!” through a window as officers approached, but received no response, according to the lawsuit. When he finally ran out the back door with both hands raised, he had already dropped the knife he was carrying in self-defense. Officers Matt Thomas and Engle Diaz opened fire, with Diaz continuing to shoot after Lyon fell, the lawsuit alleges. “You shot the wrong guy – he was holding me hostage,” Lyon told officers as he lay bleeding on the ground, according toRing doorbell camera footage cited in the lawsuit. Lyon was hospitalized for four weeks and underwent several operations, including the removal of part of his lungs, appendix and spleen. The shooting forced him to miss a semester at St. Anselm College in New Hampshire and his senior lacrosse season. He has since returned to playing but will need additional orthopedic and plastic surgery to repair his facial injuries, his attorney Alicia LeDuc Montgomery said. The incident began after Lyon's father called 911 to report that Dakota was holding his younger brother at knifepoint inside their family home. Dakota struggled with drug use following a knee injury and was living in a separate studio apartment inside his parents' home after being released from prison in November 2025. He was serving post-prison supervision for a previous assault and weapons conviction. https://www.the-independent.com/news/world/americas/crime/college-student-shot-by-cops-oregon-b3079885.html

item.title: Israel Lobby Quietly Shifts Political Operation To Super PAC Under New Name "United Democracy Project".
item.description:
The American Israel Public Affairs Committee, better known as AIPAC, plans to stop endorsing candidates, making direct PAC contributions and earmarking contributions to candidates. The shift reverses a strategy adopted five years ago as the influential pro-Israel group faces mounting political resistance. The change was disclosed Wednesday in a letter to members obtained by CNBC. AIPAC will continue operating United Democracy Project, its super PAC, while putting greater emphasis on mobilizing individual donors to give directly to candidates, according to the letter.
Jewish Insider first reported the change. “We’re looking to dramatically expand our political involvement as a community and to heighten our activists’ direct impact. That will be our focus in the next two years,” AIPAC spokesperson Deryn Sousa told CNBC in a statement. In the letter, however, the group called 2026 “one of the most challenging environments in recent memory” and warned those challenges “will continue to grow.”
A Pew Research Center survey this year found that 80% of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents held an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 53% in 2022. AIPAC has deployed about $105.1 million through its traditional PAC and affiliated super PAC this cycle, according to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings. Its United Democracy Project reported $53.4 million in independent expenditures through the end of September, according to FEC filings. AIPAC’s traditional PAC was the nation’s largest PAC contributor to candidates and other political committees in 2025, giving $26.8 million, according to FEC data. That was more than four times the $6.1 million given by the National Association of Realtors’ PAC, the next-largest contributor. AIPAC’s biggest intervention of the cycle was also a major defeat. Its United Democracy Project super PAC spent more than $30 million in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary supporting Rep. Haley Stevens and opposing Abdul El-Sayed, according to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings, but El-Sayed narrowly won the nomination. The super PAC also spent millions in House primaries opposing Democrats Cori Bush and Tom Malinowski and Republican Thomas Massie. According to a CNBC analysis of FEC filings, it spent more than $3 million in the Bush race, roughly $2.3 million against Malinowski and more than $4 million in the Kentucky primary where Massie was defeated.
United Democracy Project is a nonpartisan super PAC created to advocate for political organizations and candidates that support the United States’ partnership with Israel. The super PAC “works to help elect candidates that share our vision and will be strong supporters of the U.S.-Israel relationship in Congress,” according to its website. The American Israel Public Affairs Committee, a lobbying group established in the 1950s, historically refused to contribute funds to individual candidates’ campaigns. However, AIPAC announced its plans to launch a political action committee, or PAC, and a super PAC ahead of the 2022 election cycle in December 2021. AIPAC PAC, which was created on Dec. 15, 2021, has become the biggest pro-Israel PAC in the U.S., ahead of the Joint Action Committee for Public Affairs and JStreetPAC. United Democracy Project, AIPAC’s super PAC, was established on Jan. 3, 2022.
On June 23, Politico reported that, to hide its involvement in certain races, “United Democracy Project has shielded more than 40 percent of the money it has spent across primaries in both parties so far for the 2026 cycle through pop-up and pass-through PACs,” according to the publication’s analysis.
AIPAC has adapted to this reality. United Democracy Project has shielded more than 40 percent of the money it has spent across primaries in both parties so far for the 2026 cycle through pop-up and pass-through PACs, according to POLITICO’s analysis. “For a long time, AIPAC has had a pretty free hand. They’re still a formidable force on Capitol Hill,” Van Hollen, who has ties to another pro-Israel PAC, J Street, said on a recent press call. But, he added, “AIPAC’s position of providing unconditional American taxpayer support for the government of Israel is not a popular position.”

item.description: What was your favorite horror movie to rent at Blockbuster? And secondly, which was your favorite VHS cover to look at while browsing? You can pay $14.99 a month for Amazon Prime and still reach movie night with another rental charge waiting for you. Your membership covers the titles marked “Included with Prime.” The rest can carry a separate price, even when the movie’s been around for decades. That’s part of what makes the idea of a Blockbuster trip feel so appealing. You could make an evening out of choosing: taking your time, considering something unfamiliar, finding a snack to go with it. The anticipation belonged to movie night, too. The supplied listings put a 4K Amazon rental of 1996’s Independence Day at $3.99 and a UHD rental of 1998’s Practical Magic at $5.99. Prime doesn’t promise access to every film in the store, and a title that was included can become a separate purchase when rights arrangements change. There’s only 1 place where the name survives: the independently franchised Blockbuster in Bend, Oregon, the last remaining store since early 2020.

item.description: THE ERA OF SEALED-IN PHONE BATTERIES MAY BE COMING TO AN END! Europe is introducing new rules that could change how smartphones are designed, repaired, and used. Starting in 2027, smartphones sold in the European Union will generally need batteries that consumers can remove and replace more easily, without proprietary tools or complicated repair procedures. But that's not all. The new regulations also introduce several important requirements: 5-Year Availability: Replacement batteries must remain available for at least five years after a phone model stops being sold. 800 Charge Cycles: Smartphone batteries must generally retain at least 80% of their original capacity after 800 full charge cycles. Easier Repairs: Manufacturers will face requirements designed to make battery replacement more accessible. Less Electronic Waste: The goal is to extend smartphone lifespans, reduce unnecessary upgrades, and make repairs more practical. For years, many smartphones have featured sealed-in batteries that are difficult or expensive to replace. Europe is now pushing manufacturers toward a different approach. Starting in 2027, will smartphones become easier to repair and last longer? Would you support this change in your country?
